resale_co.name: Certificate of Continuing Occupancy (CCO), issued after the extraneous flow (sump pump / roof drain / floor drain) inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Medford Lakes (Wastewater Department inspection; Office of Construction handles CCO questions)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are scheduled based on availability. Fees are lowest when the application is filed more than 10 business days before settlement.
requirements: Sump pumps, roof drains, floor drains and other drainage devices must not be connected directly or indirectly to the Borough sanitary sewer; a CCO is issued only after any such connections are permanently removed (Code 190-26)

Disconnected sump pumps and drains must discharge at least 10 feet from any structure with a basement, cellar or crawl space, not into a street, storm sewer, neighbor's property or lake without approval
Smoke alarm, CO alarm and fire extinguisher inspection done together with the CCO inspection (see fire_cert)

fees.label: Extraneous flow (sump pump / roof / floor drain) inspection, Wastewater Department, more than 10 business days before settlement (no separate CCO fee was found)
fees.quote: More than 10 Business Days Prior to Settlement: $50

fees.label: Extraneous flow inspection, 4 to 10 business days before settlement
Extraneous flow inspection, less than 4 business days before settlement
fees.quote: Less than 4 Business Days Prior to Settlement: $125

fees.label: Cash bond if the work cannot be finished before closing (Borough then issues a temporary CCO; bond returned after approval)
fees.quote: If conditions preclude the issuance of a certificate of continuing occupancy, a cash bond in the amount of $2,000 shall be posted with the Borough to guarantee the completion of said work.

resale_co.how_to_apply: File the Application for Certificate of Extraneous Flow Elimination Compliance with the Wastewater Department (14 Stokes Road, 609-654-2013, office hours Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.) with the fee; the inspector contacts the applicant once the paid application is received. The Borough code says the property owner is responsible for scheduling this inspection. File the Fire Inspection Application at the same time. For other CCO questions contact the Office of Construction, 1 Cabin Circle, 609-654-8898 ext. 128, construction@medfordlakes.com.

evidence.quote: A certificate of continuing occupancy is required upon any sale or transfer of property to ensure that extraneous flow is not entering the sanitary sewer system.
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to schedule an inspection with the appropriate representative of the Borough of Medford Lakes.

Upon the transfer of ownership of real property, or change of use or occupancy of commercial property, or change of tenant in rental property, the Borough shall require an inspection to determine if indirect sanitary sewer connections exist.

A residential Smoke Alarm/CO Alarm/Fire Extinguisher inspection is performed in conjunction with the CCO (Certificate of Continued Occupancy) inspection. A simple application can be completed when applying for a residential CCO when selling or renting a home.
You will also need an extraneous flow inspection, this inspection insures that sump pumps, roof drains, and floor drains are not connected to the Borough wastewater system.
Tom Boyd Construction Official Sherry Rockhill-Smith Assistant to the Construction Official

resale_co.notes: Re-check 2026-10-13: the Borough Code on ecode360 (ME1961) was read this time and settles what the CCO is. Section 190-26 (Sewers, added 2002) says a certificate of continuing occupancy is required on any sale or transfer of property to make sure no extraneous flow enters the sanitary sewer, that Borough employees inspect before it is issued, and that a $2,000 cash bond allows a temporary CCO if the work cannot be done first. Section 190-18.1 (amended September 12, 2024) also requires an inspection for indirect sewer connections on every transfer of ownership. The fee schedule in Section 112-5 lists the same extraneous flow inspection fees as the Wastewater form ($50 / $70 / $125, re-inspection $35). The Borough's Rentals and Change of Occupancy page says the smoke/CO/extinguisher inspection is done together with the CCO inspection and that a simple application is completed when selling or renting a home. No separate Construction Office CCO fee or form was found, so the CCO appears to rest on the extraneous flow inspection plus the fire certificate. The Office of Construction email link on the Construction page is construction@medfordlakes.com (labeled for Sherry Rockhill-Smith, Assistant to the Construction Official). Rentals also need Landlord Registration signed by the Fire Official.

requirements: House numbers: numerals at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed to the house and visible from the street; light post or mailbox numbers are not accepted
Smoke alarm on every level; basement alarm at the bottom of the stairwell at ceiling level (not between joists); hallway alarm within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Smoke alarm on the ceiling of every bedroom in homes built 1991 to present
Hard-wired smoke alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms; all smoke alarms under 10 years old and working; battery alarms must be the 10-year battery type
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms, under 10 years old, installed per the maker; plug-in, battery or hard-wired accepted, but not in switched outlets or against floor molding
Fire extinguisher still on the October 2024 form: minimum 2A-10B:C, under 10 pounds, mounted on its bracket within 10 feet of the kitchen in the exit path, visible and reachable
Homes with a low voltage fire alarm system must have it tested and approved by the alarm company before the inspection and show the alarm certification at the inspection

authorities.name: Borough of Medford Lakes Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention (LEA #03321)
authorities.lead_time: Submit to the Borough Office more than 10 business days before settlement to avoid higher fees. The Fire Official contacts the applicant once the paid application is received. The October 2024 form says certificates are valid for 90 days; the Borough web page says six months.

fees.label: More than 10 business days before settlement
fees.quote: More than 10 Business Days Prior to Settlement: $50

fees.label: Less than 4 business days before settlement
fees.quote: Less than 4 Business Days Prior to Settlement: $125

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance (address, block and lot, owner, occupant, sales agent and firm, settlement date) and submit it with the fee, payable to the Borough of Medford Lakes, to the Borough Office at 1 Cabin Circle. The form records cash or check; the web page says cash or money order. The Fire Official then calls to schedule.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (per the Borough's October 2024 application form)

evidence.quote: The cost of the Smoke Detector/CO Detector Compliance Certificate is $50 if scheduled 10 days prior to change of occupancy, $70 if scheduled 4 to 10 days prior to change or $125 if scheduled less than 4 days prior.
Cash or Money Order are acceptable methods of payment. The Certificate issued is good for six months from the date of issuance.

Requests should be submitted to the Borough Office more than ten business days prior to the settlement date to avoid additional fees. For questions contact the Fire Official (609) 316-8584 vincent.knott@mlfd371.org
Enf Auth. Municipal Fire Official Craig Farnsworth II Phone (609) 654-8898 Email craig.farnsworth@mlfd371.org

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Medford Lakes as a municipal fire code enforcing agency (code M). Contact conflict: the Borough's Fire Inspection Application (PDF created 2024-10-30) names Vincent Knott as the Fire Official contact, with (856) 316-8584 in the header and (609) 316-8584 in the body; the DCA directory, surveyed 5/18/2026 and newer than the form, lists Fire Official Craig Farnsworth II, (609) 654-8898, craig.farnsworth@mlfd371.org, with 'Medford Lakes Boro Fire Prev', 1 Cabin Circle Dr as the Smoke Detector Compliance contact. Per the research rules the Borough's own form is used above, but the directory may be more current; the Borough office line is 609-654-8898. The 856 area code matches a number the DCA directory prints for the neighboring Lumberton entry. The web page suggests keeping the extinguisher under the kitchen sink or mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen, while the October 2024 form requires it to be mounted on its bracket; the form is used here. The web page and the form also differ on how long the certificate is valid (six months vs 90 days). The form predates P.L.2025, c.19 and still requires an extinguisher. Re-checked 2026-10-13: the Borough fee schedule (Code 112-5) lists the same Fire Official fees for 'USE Group R3/R4 Sale/Rental' ($50 at 10 business days prior, $70 at 4 to 10, $125 under 4, re-inspection $35); the form and web page are unchanged.

other_items.label: Extraneous flow elimination certificate (sump pump, roof and floor drains)
other_items.detail: This Wastewater Department inspection is the basis for the Borough's certificate of continuing occupancy on a sale (see resale_co). Same fee tiers as the fire certificate; $35 re-inspection. Wastewater Department, 14 Stokes Road, 609-654-2013.
